Is it possible to get a blazing fast 1 GB connection on a private LAN? Or do you just automatically have a fast connection because you're on a LAN?

If your router and computer NIC support 1Gbps, then yes. You'll have a 1Gbps connection. Whether the computer can actually manage that speed is something else.

You'll also need CAT-6E, not CAT-5E. Chances are really good, too, that DIY CAT6E will be problematic until cable certification testers (certify for speed, not simply test the pair matching) that can handle CAT6E drop in price.
At those speeds you might be more limited by hard drive or cpu speeds than the network itself, depending on what you're doing.

You ask a simple question but it is really a very loaded question. This blazing fast 1 GB connection on a private LAN has bottle necks. First, your computer and many pieces of that computer. Hard drive, memory, network card just to name a few. Then the cable you are sending the data on. Then the switch you are sending data through. Then all the same things in reverse order back to another machine. It is actually very hard to get 1 GB on a 1GB connection because of overhead.

You automatically have a fast connection because you are local with less overhead than sending over a WAN. WAN's are normally congested and then you throw in metered speeds and encryption you will get even less speed.
